I have no database or sequence tools in this session — no dbSNP/ClinVar/gnomAD lookup, no shell, no network. So everything below is from my own knowledge, and I've flagged the numbers you should verify before acting on them.

## The four variants

| rsID | Gene / change | Approx. population frequency | Clinical class | Effect size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rs113993960 | *CFTR* p.Phe508del (F508del/ΔF508), c.1521_1523delCTT | ~1% allele freq in non-Finnish Europeans (~1/25 carriers); rare in African/East Asian ancestry | **Pathogenic**, autosomal recessive (ClinVar: Pathogenic, many submitters, no conflict) | Mendelian — homozygotes have cystic fibrosis |
| rs429358 | *APOE* p.Cys112Arg — the ε4-defining site | ε4 ~14% in Europeans, ~20–25% in African ancestry | Established risk factor (late-onset Alzheimer's, CAA, lipids) | Large for a common variant: OR ≈ 3 het, ≈ 12–15 hom (European ancestry) |
| rs7412 | *APOE* p.Arg158Cys — the ε2-defining site | ε2 ~7–8% in Europeans | Protective for AD; ε2/ε2 predisposes to type III hyperlipoproteinaemia (low penetrance, needs a second hit) | Moderate, mostly protective |
| rs1801133 | *MTHFR* c.665C>T p.Ala222Val (the "C677T") | T allele ~25–35% Europeans, up to ~45% in some Latin American populations | **Not clinically actionable.** ACMG (2013) and ACOG explicitly recommend *against* MTHFR polymorphism testing | Tiny — modest homocysteine effect, no reliable disease association |

## The key structural point

**rs429358 and rs7412 are not two independent follow-ups — they are one assay.** Neither is interpretable alone; the ε2/ε3/ε4 haplotype is defined by the *combination* (ε3 = rs429358-T + rs7412-C; ε4 = rs429358-C; ε2 = rs7412-T). If you genotype only rs7412 you cannot distinguish ε2 carriers from ε3/ε4 configurations. So budget them as a pair, phased or at least genotyped on the same sample.

## Recommended priority

1. **rs113993960 (CFTR F508del)** — the only Mendelian, fully penetrant variant in the set. A homozygote or compound heterozygote has a diagnosis, not a risk estimate. It also carries the clearest intervention: F508del is the indication for CFTR modulator therapy (elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor), plus reproductive-carrier implications for relatives. Highest information-per-dollar by a wide margin.
2. **rs429358 + rs7412 together (APOE ε genotype)** — the largest common-variant effect in human complex disease, and now pharmacogenomically relevant: ε4 homozygosity drives ARIA risk on anti-amyloid antibodies (lecanemab, donanemab), and APOE modifies lipid and CVD risk. Caveat: it's probabilistic, has no definitive preventive action, and has real disclosure/consent weight — so it's a priority only if your study design and consent cover returning it.
3. **rs1801133 (MTHFR)** — deprioritise. It's common enough that you'll see it in essentially every cohort, and professional guidelines say testing lacks clinical utility. Spending follow-up budget here is the clearest waste of the four.

**Where this could flip:** priority depends on your phenotype. If the cohort is neurological/cognitive, APOE moves to first. If it's pulmonary, pancreatic insufficiency, or male infertility (CBAVD), CFTR is first and is also diagnostic. If it's hyperlipidaemia specifically, rs7412 gains weight because ε2/ε2 is the type III hyperlipoproteinaemia genotype. I don't know your cohort, so the ranking above assumes a general/unselected one.

**Verify before you act:** I'd check each rsID in dbSNP/ClinVar yourself for current coordinates and classification. From memory the GRCh38 positions are roughly chr7:117,559,590 (rs113993960), chr19:44,908,684 (rs429358), chr19:44,908,822 (rs7412), chr1:11,796,321 (rs1801133) — treat these as recalled, not looked up, and confirm them. The frequencies above are approximate gnomAD-scale figures from memory, not values I computed here.

## ANSWER

1. **rs113993960** (*CFTR* F508del) — pathogenic, Mendelian, therapy-actionable. Top priority.
2. **rs429358 + rs7412** — fund as a single APOE ε-genotype assay; neither is interpretable alone. Large effect, but probabilistic and consent-sensitive.
3. **rs1801133** (*MTHFR* C677T) — drop it; ACMG/ACOG advise against testing, no clinical utility.

Flips to APOE-first if the cohort is cognitive/neurological. All of the above is from my own knowledge — I had no database tools available this session.
